newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX unhappy with response to fuel oil contract.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX unhappy with response to fuel oil contract.

text.p: The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) said on Thursday it is disappointed with the slow build up of trading activities in the revised fuel oil futures contract.
It said the contract is unlikely to take off if every trader takes a wait-and-see-attitude and urged them to realise their participation as promised earlier.

"They need to realise that if everyone simply adopts the same attitude as theirs of waiting for other traders to do the work of building up liquidity, the contract is unlikely to take off," a SIMEX spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said the contract was re-launched with input and proposals from oil traders and with "clear indication" that they would take part in the market.
"We are disappointed with the slow build-up of trading in the revised fuel oil contract," he said.
SIMEX re-launched the contract on April 22, but it is still gripped by its years-old dormancy, failing to attract much support from the oil trading community.
The average daily turnover is about 40-50 lots since the re-launch. On Wednesday, about 35 100-tonne lots were traded.
Oil traders said that while SIMEX provided a better regulated market, they still prefered to trade on the swaps market or the over-the-counter market where trade is much more volatile and liquid.

The fuel oil contract was first listed on SIMEX in 1989 and it traded at a peak of 5,000 contracts per day. But the volume gradually fell, hitting 162 lots in August 1995, and was untraded since October 1996 before the relaunch.
